question: Which AI agents create the most value?
html:
Which AI agents create the most value

The largest value is at Thomas Scientific (est. $3.8M) and Frontline (est. $3.6M), together about 58% of the est. $12.7M portfolio total. By rollout stage, wave 3 revenue agents lead at est. $4.2M. The context does not rank individual agents, because it shows values for only two of 61 items. (Portfolio AI-agent plan)

Value by portfolio company

Each company's total sits inside its ServiceOS roadmap range (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Value by rollout wave

  • Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents: est. $2.8M.
  • Wave 2, finance agents: est. $3.9M.
  • Wave 3, revenue agents: est. $4.2M. This is the largest wave.
  • Wave 4, monitoring services: est. $1.8M.

Wave 1 is smaller, but it has the clearest baselines and the lowest risk (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Strongest single-agent evidence

  • Punctual Pros' missed-call and after-hours booking agent has the most worked model. It shows an est. $1.37M a year of recovered revenue (Voice AI research).
  • Outbound membership renewal adds an est. $403k of revenue on an assumed 6,000 members (Voice AI research).
  • These figures are revenue, not EBITDA-equivalent. They are not comparable to the $0.88M Punctual Pros agent total.

Caveats

  • Every value is a labelled analyst assumption. Volumes such as calls, tickets and invoices must be replaced with system-of-record counts (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • The totals are not de-duplicated, so overlapping agents may double-count value.
  • Most claimed metrics come from vendor case studies, which are self-reported and unaudited (Voice AI research).
  • A true agent-level ranking needs the estimated value field for all 61 plan items, sorted and de-duplicated.

Next actions

  1. Pull the full 61-item agent list. Rank it by estimated annual value and flag overlaps that need de-duplication.
  2. Replace assumed volumes at Thomas Scientific and Frontline with system counts first, since they carry about 58% of the value.
  3. Pull Punctual Pros' actual call logs, missed-call rate and membership count. Use them to validate the wave 1 missed-call model before rollout.
  4. Restate the revenue figures in the voice model on the same EBITDA-equivalent basis as the agent plan.

# Which AI agents create the most value

**The largest value is at Thomas Scientific (est. $3.8M) and Frontline (est. $3.6M), together about 58% of the est. $12.7M portfolio total. By rollout stage, wave 3 revenue agents lead at est. $4.2M. The context does not rank individual agents, because it shows values for only two of 61 items.** (Portfolio AI-agent plan)

## Value by portfolio company

| Portfolio company | Est. annual value | Share of total | Roadmap range |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thomas Scientific | $3.84M | ~30% | $1.25-4.8M |
| Frontline | $3.59M | ~28% | $1.5-4.2M |
| BPI | $2.27M | ~18% | $0.85-3.75M |
| CET | $1.32M | ~10% | $0.62-2.62M |
| Punctual Pros | $0.88M | ~7% | $0.32-1.12M |
| Fair Harbor | $0.77M | ~6% | $0.40-1.75M |

Each company's total sits inside its ServiceOS roadmap range (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Value by rollout wave

- Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents: est. $2.8M.
- Wave 2, finance agents: est. $3.9M.
- Wave 3, revenue agents: est. $4.2M. This is the largest wave.
- Wave 4, monitoring services: est. $1.8M.

Wave 1 is smaller, but it has the clearest baselines and the lowest risk (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Strongest single-agent evidence

- Punctual Pros' missed-call and after-hours booking agent has the most worked model. It shows an est. $1.37M a year of recovered *revenue* (Voice AI research).
- Outbound membership renewal adds an est. $403k of revenue on an assumed 6,000 members (Voice AI research).
- These figures are revenue, not EBITDA-equivalent. They are not comparable to the $0.88M Punctual Pros agent total.

## Caveats

- Every value is a labelled analyst assumption. Volumes such as calls, tickets and invoices must be replaced with system-of-record counts (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
- The totals are not de-duplicated, so overlapping agents may double-count value.
- Most claimed metrics come from vendor case studies, which are self-reported and unaudited (Voice AI research).
- A true agent-level ranking needs the estimated value field for all 61 plan items, sorted and de-duplicated.

## Next actions

1. Pull the full 61-item agent list. Rank it by estimated annual value and flag overlaps that need de-duplication.
2. Replace assumed volumes at Thomas Scientific and Frontline with system counts first, since they carry about 58% of the value.
3. Pull Punctual Pros' actual call logs, missed-call rate and membership count. Use them to validate the wave 1 missed-call model before rollout.
4. Restate the revenue figures in the voice model on the same EBITDA-equivalent basis as the agent plan.
